players.note: Jordan Love is the QB12 in fantasy points per game. It was nice to see that in Josh Jacobs' first game back, Green Bay didn't dial back their passing rate. In Weeks 1-6, Green Bay had a 65.9% pass rate, and last week they actually bumped it a tad higher to 70.8%. Overall, they have the second-best passing rate in the NFL. Among 34 qualifying passers, Love has still struggled with accuracy, ranking 22nd in passing success rate and 28th in catchable target rate, but he is also tenth in hero throw rate and 14th in passing touchdown rate. This week, Love will have a tougher matchup. Since Week 4, Carolina has continued to field a strong pass defense, allowing the 11th-fewest yards per attempt, the eighth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the 13th-lowest passing success rate. Love has the volume, the talent, and the skilled receivers to overcome a strong pass defense.

Matthew Stafford is the QB15 in fantasy points per game, as it has been a roller coaster ride some weeks with Stafford. He has three games with at least 22.9 fantasy points while also logging three outings with less than 17 fantasy points. Among 34 qualifying passers, Stafford is 17th in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, 18th in highly accurate throw rate, and 19th in catchable target rate. Stafford could post another QB1 week against the Bolts. Over their last five games, the Bolts have allowed the tenth-most yards per attempt, the 15th-lowest passing success rate, and ranked 16th in passing touchdown rate allowed. It's a middle-of-the-road matchup for Stafford.

Jacoby Brissett is the QB22 in fantasy points per game with two outings this season with at least 25 fantasy points. Among 34 qualifying passers, Brissett is 32nd in yards per attempt, 18th in passing success rate, tenth in highly accurate throw rate, and 14th in catchable target rate. Brissett could return to the friendly confines of QB1 land this week. Across their last five games, Dallas has allowed the sixth-most yards per attempt, the 14th-highest passing touchdown rate, the sixth-highest CPOE, and the sixth-most EPA per dropback.

Caleb Williams is the QB6 in fantasy points per game. Since returning from his hamstring injury, Williams has averaged only 10.5 rushing yards, so I don't see that being a huge part of his game this week. If his hamstring is back to 100%, maybe he surprises me, though. Among 34 qualifying passers, Williams is fifth in yards per attempt, fifth in passing success rate, second in highly accurate throw rate, and first in catchable target rate. He is having a wonderful season as he has improved his accuracy. This will be a huge test for how much he has grown this week. Seattle's pass defense is a buzz saw. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the third-fewest yards per attempt, the sixth-lowest passing success rate, the tenth-lowest CPOE, and the third-lowest EPA per dropback. In most leagues, despite the horrible matchup, you're still starting Williams.

Jared Goff has been crushing it this season as the QB3 in fantasy points per game. Among 34 qualifying passers, Goff is eighth in yards per attempt, fourth in passing touchdown rate and passing success rate, third in hero throw rate, and sixth in catchable target rate. Goff will have to deal with a Minnesota pass defense that has been easily the best pass defense in the NFL. Ok, fine, Seattle is also in that convo, but Minny has been amazing. Over the last five games, Minny has allowed the fewest yards per attempt, the lowest passing success rate, and the lowest passing touchdown rate. Overall, Minnesota has created havoc weekly, leading the NFL in blitz rate and pressure rate. Goff has navigated the blitz well this season, but he will have to be elite in this regard this week. Among 29 qualifying passers, Goff has been quite good against the blitz, ranking sixth in yards per attempt and third in passing success rate. Goff could get it done this week, but there's a sizable range of outcomes for him this week.

Kyler Murray has been a disaster at quarterback this season as the QB34 in fantasy points per game. He has run more in his last two games, averaging 7.5 attempts and 45 yards on the ground, but in the passing department he has been wretched. Among 34 qualifying passers, he is 23rd in yards per attempt, 31st in passing success rate, 28th in aDOT, and dead last in highly accurate throw rate. Murray could have a nice game this week, but I don't have any faith in him to take advantage of a nice matchup. Across their last five games, Detroit has allowed the fifth-highest passing touchdown rate, the third-highest passing success rate, the fourth-highest passer rating, and the ninth-highest CPOE. Detroit in that span also has the fourth-best pressure rate and has ranked 12th in quick pressure rate. If Detroit's pass rush can rattle Murray this week, it could be his undoing.

Even after last week's stinker, Bryce Young is the QB8 in fantasy points per game. Last week, Young completed only 51.8% of his passes with 163 passing yards (6.4 yards per attempt), a 69.6% catchable throw rate, and two picks. Overall, Young (among 34 qualifying passers) is 13th in yards per attempt, 19th in passing success rate, 26th in catchable throw rate, and 12th in hero throw rate. If Young is going to bounce back this week, he'll have to do so against a solid Green Bay pass defense. Since Week 3, Green Bay has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per attempt, the fourth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the seventh-lowest CPOE. Green Bay during that stretch also has had the 12th-lowest pressure rate, so Young should have clean pockets this week. It's a good litmus test matchup to see if Young has turned back into a pumpkin prior to Halloween.

Patrick Mahomes II has been slumping. As the QB17 in fantasy points per game, he hasn't had more than 17 fantasy points in any game since Week 2. Among 34 qualifying passers, he is tenth in yards per attempt, sixth in passing success rate, 18th in passing touchdown rate, and 23rd in highly accurate throw rate. Mahomes hasn't thrown for a touchdown since Week 4. I don't see this week as the matchup where Mahomes turns it around. Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the ninth-lowest passing success rate, and the third-lowest fantasy points per dropback.

Kirk Cousins is the QB11 in fantasy points per game as he leads the NFL in passing touchdowns (16). Among 34 qualifying passers, he is third in passing yards, 14th in yards per attempt, 22nd in highly accurate throw rate, 27th in catchable target rate, and 22nd in hero throw rate. Cousins should have another QB1 outing this week. Across their last five games, the Jets have allowed the 13th-most yards per attempt, the eighth-highest passing touchdown rate, the fifth-highest passing success rate, and the seventh-most EPA per dropback.

Sam Darnold has been a ghost for most of the season as the QB27 in fantasy points per game. In his last four games, he has had more than 15 fantasy points in any game. That could easily change this week. Among 34 qualifying passers, Darnold is 15th in yards per attempt, 21st in passing success rate, 13th in highly accurate throw rate, and fourth in catchable target rate. Darnold is a strong streamer this week. He could easily post a QB1 stat line this week. Over their last five games, Chicago has allowed the most yards per attempt, the seventh-highest passing touchdown rate, and the fifth-highest passer rating.

Geno Smith is a solid streaming option at quarterback this week. Smith is the QB24 in fantasy points per game with two games of at least 24 fantasy points this season. He could add a third game to that ledger this week. Among 34 qualifying passers, Smith has been playing well, ranking ninth in yards per attempt, 12th in passing success rate, second in catchable target rate, and eighth in hero throw rate. In their last five games, the Raiders have allowed the eighth-most yards per attempt, the second-highest passing success rate, the highest passing touchdown rate, and the fifth-most EPA per dropback.

Last week, Baker Mayfield posted only 6.7 fantasy points (QB26) in his return to the huddle. Mayfield's thumb obviously isn't 100%. He threw the ball only 11 times for 64 passing yards (5.8 yards per attempt) and a passing score. With those 11 passing attempts, Mayfield had an aDOT of 4.67 (third-lowest) and a 2.49 average time to throw (seventh-lowest). Despite the short area passing approach, Mayfield had only 36.4% of his throws deemed as highly accurate. With Tampa Bay protecting Mayfield with limited passing volume, it's impossible to feel good about plugging him into a fantasy lineup. Across their last five games, Atlanta has allowed the 13th-fewest yards per attempt, the tenth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the 14th-lowest EPA per dropback. During that span, the Falcons also have the 13th-best pressure rate and the ninth-best quick pressure rate. I expect another down week for Mayfield.

Aaron Rodgers is the QB19 in fantasy points per game with three outings this season with at least 22 fantasy points. He had a letdown game against the Saints that I didn't see coming. Among 34 qualifying passers, Rodgers is 24th in yards per attempt, 13th in passing touchdown rate, 24th in passing success rate, 19th in highly accurate throw rate, and 25th in hero throw rate. Rodgers is a low-end QB2 this week with a bad matchup. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per attempt, the 11th-lowest passing touchdown rate, the fifth-lowest passing success rate, and the 11th-lowest EPA per dropback.

Malik Willis has had 20.9 and 26 fantasy points over his last two games, as he has started to flash the fantasy upside I forecasted in the summer. Willis had a rushing score in each game while averaging eight carries and 55.5 rushing yards. Since Week 5, among 33 qualifying passers, Willis has ranked 14th in yards per attempt, sixth in passing success rate, 30th in catchable target rate, and third in fantasy points per dropback. Willis could post another QB1 stat line this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the fifth-most yards per attempt, the 11th-highest passing touchdown rate, and the eighth-highest passing success rate.

Michael Penix is the QB18 in fantasy points per game after ripping off back-to-back QB1 outings (QB5, QB8). Among 34 qualifying passers, Penix is seventh in yards per attempt, 11th in passing success rate, 17th in catchable target rate, and 16th in hero throw rate. He has played far better than I anticipated this season. Penix could log another QB1 outing this week, but it's better to view him as a mid-range QB2. Tampa Bay's pass defense has been rounding into form. Across their last five games, they have allowed the tenth-fewest yards per attempt, the eighth-lowest passing success rate, the second-lowest EPA per dropback, and the 13th-lowest passing touchdown rate.

Deshaun Watson is the QB22 in fantasy points per game with two QB1 weekly finishes on the ledger for 2026 (QB10, QB11). Among 34 qualifying passers, he is 18th in yards per attempt, 26th in passing touchdown rate, 17th in passing success rate, 15th in highly accurate throw rate, and 21st in hero throw rate. He has averaged 6.9 rushing attempts and 30.7 yards on the ground with one rushing score. He's a middling QB2 again this week. Over their last five games, Pittsburgh has allowed the 11th-fewest yards per attempt, the seventh-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the eighth-lowest CPOE.

Last week, Bo Nix flashed a fantasy pulse as the QB3 for the week. Much of that fantasy output was based on his seven carries and 73 yards (one score) on the ground, not his passing prowess. For a quarterback that, outside of last week's game, hasn't had more than ten rushing yards in any game, I don't think we can count on the rushing floor and upside weekly. Nix finished with 222 yards through the air with one touchdown, a 51.7% completion percentage, and 7.7 yards per attempt. Among 34 qualifying passers, Nix is 31st in yards per attempt, 33rd in passing success rate, 27th in passing touchdown rate, and 24th in highly accurate throw rate. I expect Nix to come back to Earth this week as a middling QB2. In their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the 14th-lowest yards per attempt, the second-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the tenth-lowest passing success rate.

Justin Herbert has been a fantasy dud all year as the QB27 in fantasy points per game. He hasn't had more than 14.3 fantasy points in any game this season. Among 34 qualifying passers, Herbert has the ninth-lowest yards per attempt, the fifth-lowest passing touchdown rate (tied with Baker Mayfield), and the third-fewest fantasy points per dropback (tied with Jalon Daniels). I don't really care what the matchup is right now for Herbert. He has been commanding a broken offense. I need to see him actually post a decent stat line before I'd plug him into a fantasy lineup. Sit him again this week.

Over the last two games, Tanner McKee has been the QB21 and QB22 in fantasy points per game. Among 40 qualifying passers, he is bottom of the barrel, ranking 39th in yards per attempt, passing success rate, and catchable target rate. Despite a promising matchup this week, McKee couldn't take advantage of a struggling Dallas secondary last week, so I have zero faith that he'll be able to do much against Washington this week. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the sixth-highest passing touchdown rate, the tenth-highest passing success rate, and the sixth-highest passer rating.

Daniel Jones has been a disaster this season. He doesn't have a single game with at least 275 passing yards or multiple passing touchdowns this season. Jones has one game with more than 15 rushing yards. I'm not surprised by the lack of ground game from Jones coming off the Achilles, but the fact that he is a statue who also can't throw the ball is a problem. Among 34 qualifying passers, Jones has the fourth-fewest yards per attempt, the 12th-lowest passing success rate, the fourth-lowest catchable target rate, and the fifth-highest off-target rate. Jones has finished higher than QB22 in weekly scoring only once this season (QB16 last week). Jones could have a decent yardage outing, but I don't see him stacking multiple touchdowns this week. Across their last five games, Jacksonville has allowed the seventh-most yards per attempt, the 14th-highest CPOE, and ranked 17th in passing success rate, but they have held passers to the eighth-lowest passing touchdown rate. Jones is a low-end QB2 again this week.

Cam Ward still barely has a pulse for fantasy as the QB36 in fantasy points per game. He has failed to eclipse 12 fantasy points in five games this season. Among 34 qualifying passers, he is 33rd in yards per attempt, 28th in passing success rate, and 33rd in passing touchdown rate and fantasy points per dropback. Until any of this changes, I'm not starting Ward in any format. He's still live to get benched in any game until this level of play changes.
